statement_en: What fraction of the night does a zebrafish larva spend asleep: 58% or 84%? And is "sleep fraction" a measurable property of the animal at all, independent of the movement criterion used to define it?
found_by: Harvested from sim-engine/scenarios/BEHAVIOUR.md, which reports the two values side by side and states that it never mixes them. The repository classifies it explicitly as a definitional rather than an empirical disagreement.

arms.statement_en: Larval night sleep is 58.2%, under the criterion of six or more consecutive seconds of non-movement.

evidence.claim: Night sleep is 58.17% for larvae under a 6-second non-movement criterion, applied at every age by one study.
evidence.source: Sorribes A et al. 2013, Front Neural Circuits 7:178, doi:10.3389/fncir.2013.00178, PMC3826060
evidence.quote: after six or more consecutive 1-s bins of non-movement, the seventh second and above were classified as sleep
evidence.kind: measurement, full text read; the one study applying the same criterion at every age

evidence.claim: A speed-threshold criterion gives a far higher value in the same animal and stage, which counts against 58% as the sleep fraction.
evidence.quote: Choudhary 2026: sleep (speed < 0.5 mm/s for >= 1 min) "accounted for 19.6 +- 1.0% of daytime and 83.9 +- 1.5% of nighttime", larvae 5-8 dpf, 14:10 LD, reared at 28 C

arms.statement_en: Larval night sleep is 83.9%, under the criterion of speed below 0.5 mm/s for at least one minute.

evidence.claim: Sleep accounted for 83.9 +- 1.5% of the night in 5-8 dpf larvae under a speed threshold.
evidence.quote: Choudhary 2026: sleep (speed < 0.5 mm/s for >= 1 min) "accounted for 19.6 +- 1.0% of daytime and 83.9 +- 1.5% of nighttime", larvae 5-8 dpf, 14:10 LD, reared at 28 C

evidence.claim: The pixel-threshold criterion gives 58.2% in the same stage, which counts against 84% as the sleep fraction.
evidence.source: Sorribes A et al. 2013, Front Neural Circuits 7:178, doi:10.3389/fncir.2013.00178, PMC3826060
evidence.quote: after six or more consecutive 1-s bins of non-movement, the seventh second and above were classified as sleep

arms.position: definition-dependence (a named alternative, not a side)
arms.statement_en: Neither number is wrong and no measurement will reconcile them: a speed threshold counts slow drifting as sleep and a pixel threshold does not, so "sleep fraction" is a property of the criterion as much as of the animal. Any law or scenario using a sleep fraction must name its criterion.

evidence.claim: The repository states the mechanism of the disagreement and classifies it as definitional, not empirical.
evidence.source: this repository (behaviour scenario thread), reading both full texts
evidence.quote: **Why the two disagree.** A speed threshold counts slow drifting as sleep and a pixel threshold does not, so the larval night comes out at 83.9% under one definition and 58.2% under the other. This is the W7 mismatch. Even with the same nominal 6 s criterion, two labs give adults 33.4% and 58.1%.

evidence.claim: Two laboratories using the SAME nominal 6-second criterion still disagree 1.7x on adults, so criterion alone does not fix the number either.
evidence.source: Sorribes 2013 vs Yokogawa T et al. 2007, PLoS Biol 5:e277, doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.0050277, PMC2020497
evidence.quote: - **Adult night, same 6 s criterion, two labs: disagree 1.7x.** Sorribes gives 33.4% and Yokogawa 58.1%. Both are shown; neither is a prediction.
evidence.kind: a second, nested disagreement that holds the criterion fixed

exclusivity.statement: The two measured arms are NOT contradictory: they measure different quantities that share a name. The repository treats them that way already ("Two sleep definitions are reported side by side and never mixed"), and the decisive evidence for arm `definition-dependent` is the nested result that two laboratories using the SAME nominal 6-second criterion still differ 1.7x on adults (33.4% vs 58.1%) -- so the criterion does not determine the number either, and a single reported "sleep fraction" is underdetermined even with its definition attached. This is the one question here where no new measurement of the headline quantity can settle the headline disagreement.
exclusivity.premise: That "sleep fraction" names one quantity independent of the movement criterion. Only under that premise do the readings conflict.

what_would_settle_it.observation: Both criteria applied to ONE recording.
what_would_settle_it.how: Score one set of larval night recordings under both the 6-second non-movement criterion and the <0.5 mm/s-for-1-minute criterion, and publish both numbers plus the conversion between them.
what_would_settle_it.why_decisive: It converts the disagreement into a known mapping between two defined quantities, which is the only thing that can be settled here. It would also test whether the 58/84 gap is wholly definitional or partly a cohort or rearing difference.
what_would_settle_it.feasibility_note: Needs only reanalysis of existing video at sufficient spatial resolution to compute speed; no new experiment.

what_would_settle_it.observation: An independent physiological marker of sleep state in a larva.
what_would_settle_it.how: Pair behavioural scoring with a non-behavioural readout (arousal threshold, or the eye-movement substates Choudhary et al. 2026 describe) and ask which behavioural criterion tracks it.
what_would_settle_it.why_decisive: It would ground "asleep" in something other than a movement threshold, making one criterion a better proxy than the other rather than merely different. Without it, neither sign of the disagreement can be called correct.

known_gaps: lean/Delphi/Perturb.lean section 6 records that there is NO Lean sleep law at all: "The only quantitative theory fetched (Savage and West 2007, PMID 17215372) is for mammals (96 species) and predicts sleep time from brain mass; no source gives a quantitative sleep law for a teleost". So this question currently touches no law, and that is deliberate.

proportion.note: share = this arm's belief / the sum over arms. Belief is E*(1-R) from the INDRA SimpleScorer form over the arm's OWN evidence; belief-params.json says plainly that its rand/syst values are hand-set and NOT fitted, so treat a share as an ordering of the arms, not a probability that an arm is true.

history.change: harvested from the sourced prose already in this repository by the open-questions thread; arms, evidence with verbatim quotes, computed belief proportion and what-would-settle-it recorded
